brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Seamline, the open-source command-line tool in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: precise, trustworthy, developer-native; it must work in a terminal-heavy README, as a GitHub avatar and on a small docs site. No database cylinders, no elephants, no generic terminal prompt. Web and GitHub only.

claim.notes: No concept passed the critic gate after two rounds (running-stitch blind distinctiveness/memorability 4, present: no; handoff and reversible-s dropped at sketch review), so nothing was finalized, exported or gallery-built.

concepts.title: Handoff
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s5 a paperclip end or magnet hook; s6 a hamburger menu or the glyph 王 with rounded bars; s7 a loading spinner or donut, the generic ring device. s1-s4 still read as offset or overlapping squares and a cut square, the stock cut devices. Nothing reaches distinctiveness 7. Direction dropped.

concepts.title: Reversible S
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s5 a square cut on its diagonal and slid apart (the stock cut device); s6 a letter N or a ribbon knot, a different letter; s7 a lightning zigzag or broken bar, thin and diagonal, which leaves the avatar mostly empty and turns to a scribble at 16 px. The S never reads first in any sketch. Older s1 reads as a 2 or a Greek key. Direction dropped.

concepts.title: Running Stitch
readsAs: a road seen from above with dashed lane markings
a perforated ticket or coupon tear line
a two-column split-view UI icon (unfortunate: a ticket/coupon or generic layout toggle in a GitHub UI)
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s5 two solid blocks laced together across a seam, ownable and on-name, and it fills the avatar tile; s6 a square cut on its diagonal (cut cliché); s7 the UI chain-link icon. Keep s5. Fix: make it read as stitches rather than ladder rungs or an H crossbar. Use 3 stitches with a clear slant and rounded ends that cross the gap with visible overlap into each half. Keep the gap narrow so the halves read as one tile. Check the 16 px render keeps 3 distinct stitches; drop to 2 if they merge. Clearly separate from pgroll and Atlas: no letterform, no geometric globe.
